idiom_name: Alpakka Kafka: raw-byte consumption with stage diversion (alsoTo an error topic) and RestartSource backoff
implementation_notes: Alpakka Kafka documents the shape precisely: a deserialization problem fails the stage immediately, so the recommended approach is to consume raw byte arrays and deserialize in a later map stage, where supervision can skip or divert failed elements, while RestartSource.onFailuresWithBackoff keeps the stream itself alive. The invalid channel becomes a second sink on that stage - an alsoTo branch that produces the original record to an error topic - so the main flow stays typed and the evidence stays intact. The receiver-side structure is absorbed into the stream topology; only the diversion decision remains application code.
code_sketch:
val decoded = Consumer.plainSource(settings, Subscriptions.topics("orders"))
  .map(rec => (decode(rec.value()), rec))         // (Either[DecodeError, Order], record)

decoded.collect { case (Left(_), rec) =>
  new ProducerRecord[Array[Byte], Array[Byte]]("orders.invalid", rec.value()) }
  .runWith(Producer.plainSink(errorSettings))

decoded.collect { case (Right(order), _) => order }
  .via(businessFlow)
  .runWith(Sink.ignore)
pitfalls: Letting the stage fail (instead of diverting) tears down the whole stream under the default supervision strategy, so one malformed record stops every valid message behind it.
recover and recoverWithRetries drop elements unless they are paired with a sink that records them - recovery without an error channel is exactly the black hole the pattern forbids.
In at-least-once mode the offset commit must happen after the error topic has confirmed the write, or the invalid record disappears at the next rebalance.
